  - text: CLASS 11 · RELATIONS AND FUNCTIONS
  - heading "Invertible Functions" [level=1]
  - paragraph: Build a function from finite sets, test for one-one and onto, flip arrows to get the inverse, and verify the inverse property.
  - navigation: ◷ 18 min ADVANCED CONCEPT graph
  - button "Reset lab":
    - img
    - text: Reset lab
  - main:
    - 'heading "1. BUILD A FUNCTION f : A → B" [level=2]':
      - text: 1. BUILD A FUNCTION
      - emphasis: "f : A → B"
    - button "Edit sets":
      - img
      - text: Edit sets
    - article:
      - heading "A (Domain)" [level=3]
      - button "1"
      - button "2"
      - button "3"
    - img "Forward function arrows"
    - article:
      - heading "B (Codomain)" [level=3]
      - button "a"
      - button "b"
      - button "c"
    - heading "2. MINI GRAPH (x, f(x))" [level=2]:
      - text: 2. MINI GRAPH
      - emphasis: (x, f(x))
    - img "Finite function mini graph"
    - heading "3. TESTS FOR INVERTIBILITY" [level=2]
    - article:
      - text: ONE-ONE (Injective)
      - strong: PASS ✓
      - paragraph: Every element in B has at most one preimage.
      - text: a b c
    - article:
      - text: ONTO (Surjective)
      - strong: PASS ✓
      - paragraph: Every element in B has at least one preimage.
      - text: a b c
    - button "Flip Arrows f⁻¹":
      - img
      - text: Flip Arrows f⁻¹
    - text: — Mapping — Collision (not one-one) — Uncovered (not onto)
    - complementary: Both tests pass. The inverse is a function.
    - article:
      - 'heading "4. INVERSE FUNCTION f⁻¹ : B → A" [level=2]'
      - text: Auto
      - switch "Automatic inverse" [checked]
      - text: a b c
      - img
      - text: 1 2 3 f⁻¹(a) = 1 f⁻¹(b) = 2 f⁻¹(c) = 3
    - article:
      - 'heading "5. VERIFY: x → f(x) → f⁻¹(f(x)) = x" [level=2]'
      - paragraph:
        - text: 1 → a →
        - emphasis: "1"
        - img
      - paragraph:
        - text: 2 → b →
        - emphasis: "2"
        - img
      - paragraph:
        - text: 3 → c →
        - emphasis: "3"
        - img
    - article:
      - heading "6. INVERSE-PAIR TABLE" [level=2]
      - table:
        - rowgroup:
          - row "x ∈ A f(x) ∈ B f⁻¹(f(x)) Result":
            - columnheader "x ∈ A"
            - columnheader "f(x) ∈ B"
            - columnheader "f⁻¹(f(x))"
            - columnheader "Result"
        - rowgroup:
          - row "1 a 1 ✓":
            - cell "1"
            - cell "a"
            - cell "1"
            - cell "✓"
          - row "2 b 2 ✓":
            - cell "2"
            - cell "b"
            - cell "2"
            - cell "✓"
          - row "3 c 3 ✓":
            - cell "3"
            - cell "c"
            - cell "3"
            - cell "✓"
      - text: ✓ All good! f is invertible and f⁻¹ is its inverse.
  - complementary:

    - text: "Best classroom move: if either test fails, ask learners to adjust the mapping and try again. Both must PASS to get an inverse."
